Data source

or choose a file

.xlsx or .csv with columns p, Np, Gp, Bo, Rs, Bg, and time if you have it

What the file needs
  • A table with a header row: pressure p, Np, Gp (or Rp), Bo, Rs and Bg, in any order. Units in the header, like “Np (MMSTB)”, are read.
  • The initial parameters pi, Boi, Bgi, Rsi, Swc, Cw, Cf as label and value pairs, on a second sheet or beside or below the table.
  • If Boi, Bgi or Rsi are missing, they are read from the table row at pi.
  • Optional columns: time (t in years, months or days, or dates), water produced Wp, and water influx We if you know it. Time lets the dashboard test steady- and unsteady-state aquifers.
  • For oil above its bubble point, Rs, Bg and Gp can be left out.
  • The file stays on your computer. Nothing is uploaded.

              Calculation table

              Every term of the material balance at each pressure, in field units. Untick a row to leave it out of the fit.

              Method

              Havlena and Odeh (1963) wrote the material balance as a straight line, one for each drive mechanism. The dashboard uses them to find the mechanism in three steps.

              1. Depletion check. With depletion alone, the apparent N = F / (Eo + Efw) is the same at every step. If it drifts, more energy is acting.
              2. Fit every mechanism. Depletion: F against Et through the origin. Gas cap: the straight line below, with N as the intercept and mN as the slope. Water drive: F/Et against We/Et, a line of slope 1 that meets the axis at N, with a pot, steady-state or unsteady-state aquifer. Gas cap and water drive together. The aquifer constants are found by least squares, which does the trial and error for you.
              3. Keep what the data support. A model counts only if N, m and the aquifer constant are positive, each mechanism in it supplies at least 2 % of F, and their signs survive rounding the table within its last digit (90 % of 120 trials). Of those, the one with the lowest AICc (Akaike’s criterion, corrected for few points) on the relative misfit of F wins; within 2 of it, the one with fewer constants wins. Without a time column, steady- and unsteady-state aquifers are tried only when nothing simpler fits, with the rows taken as equal time steps.
              Underground withdrawal
              F=Np [Bo+(Rp−Rs) Bg]+Wp Bw
              Oil and dissolved gas
              Eo=(Bo−Boi)+(Rsi−Rs) Bg
              Gas-cap expansion
              Eg=Boi (BgBgi−1)
              Connate water and rock
              Efw=Boi Cw Swc+Cf1−Swc Δp
              Material balance
              F=N [Eo+m Eg+(1+m) Efw]+We
              Straight line
              F−WeEo+(1+m) Efw=N+mN EgEo+(1+m) Efw
              Gas cap from the line
              m=slopeinterceptG=mN BoiBgi
              Drive indices
              DDI=N EoFSDI=N m EgFCDI=N (1+m) EfwFWDI=WeF
              Depletion
              F=N Et,Et=Eo+m Eg+(1+m) Efw
              Water drive

              Units used in the calculation: p in psia, Np in STB, Gp in SCF, Rs and Rp in SCF/STB, Bo in rb/STB, Bg in rb/SCF (ft³/SCF ÷ 5.615), Cw and Cf in psi⁻¹. t in days. Values in other units are converted first. The 95 % ranges come from the least-squares fit; the range of m uses the delta method.
